layer1_evidence.interpretation_en: A 69-year-old woman had a right middle-lobe subpleural nodule followed for more than 10 years with gradual enlargement and was admitted for surgical treatment; she had no obvious respiratory symptoms.

The preoperative assessment found an indication for surgery for the right middle-lobe nodule without obvious contraindications; thoracoscopic resection and intraoperative management of lymph nodes and pleural adhesions were planned.

On postoperative day 1, the patient had incisional pain, cough with sputum, and nausea but no dyspnea and a normal temperature; chest-drain output was approximately 135 mL, and respiratory care, drainage monitoring, and symptomatic treatment remained necessary.

The preoperative CT, reviewed only after surgery, showed tiny nodules in both lungs, with the dominant nodule near the pleura of the right middle lobe adjacent to the oblique fissure and approximately unchanged from prior imaging, plus chronic pleural thickening and adhesions; the additional nodules require documentation and assessment, but progression or metastasis cannot be inferred.
The postoperative chest radiograph assessed right-lung postoperative changes and chest-drain status, with no documented indication for immediate reoperation.

Frozen section of the right middle-lobe nodule showed atypical alveolar epithelial hyperplasia, considered adenocarcinoma in situ; the stapled margin was free of carcinoma, but final paraffin pathology is not yet available and cannot be replaced by the frozen assessment.

Thoracoscopic partial resection of the right middle lobe, intrathoracic lymph-node dissection, and lysis of pleural adhesions were completed, with a chest drain left in place; the operative record explicitly states partial resection.
